description: Curated multimodal evaluation suite using real Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 optical imagery from BigEarthNet-MM to evaluate real-data loading, grid alignment, and multimodal VLM reasoning quality.

dataset_provenance.source_dataset: BigEarthNet-MM (Multi-Modal BigEarthNet Benchmark, Sumbul et al., 2021)
dataset_provenance.optical_sensor: Sentinel-2A MSI (Multi-Spectral Instrument), Level-2A Bottom-Of-Atmosphere reflectance
dataset_provenance.sar_sensor: Sentinel-1B SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar), C-band Interferometric Wide (IW) swath Ground Range Detected High resolution (GRDH)
dataset_provenance.license: Community Data License Agreement - Permissive (CDLA-Permissive) / Copernicus Open Access Policy
dataset_provenance.geographic_region: Upper Austria / Bavaria border region, Tile 33UUP
dataset_provenance.spatial_reference: WGS 84 / UTM Zone 33N (EPSG:32633), native 10m spatial resolution
dataset_provenance.alignment_policy: Aligned to a common optical reference grid. Reprojection ensures spatial overlap and identical pixel geometry; sub-pixel co-registration is not claimed without empirical cross-correlation.

cases.question: Use the optical and SAR images together to identify likely built-up areas.
cases.expected_focus: optical reflectance/texture + SAR backscatter / urban double-bounce cues + uncertainty where ambiguous
cases.notes: Real multimodal observation over rural Upper Austria. High localized SAR returns (up to +0.5 dB) might indicate small agricultural structures or tree clumps, but optical texture confirms predominantly rural vegetation. Evaluates whether model avoids hallucinating dense urban fabric while noting localized structure ambiguity.

cases.question: Use the optical and SAR imagery together to identify water-covered regions.
cases.expected_focus: optical water appearance + SAR low-return/specular-reflection behavior where applicable
cases.notes: Tests water recognition on a non-aquatic rural scene. The model should check both optical reflectance (lack of water absorption/cyan signature) and SAR specular reflection (absence of flat dark specular radar returns) and conclude that open water bodies are absent.

cases.question: Describe the dominant vegetation patterns using both optical and SAR evidence.
cases.expected_focus: optical vegetation appearance + SAR structural/volume-scattering cues
cases.notes: Evaluates optical greenness/crop reflectance combined with SAR volume-scattering signatures (elevated VH cross-polarization in forest canopy vs. lower returns over pastures and arable fields).

cases.question: What information does SAR provide that is less apparent in the optical image?
cases.notes: Explicit comparative cross-modal reasoning. Optical provides surface color, pigment absorption, and visible boundaries; SAR provides structural roughness, geometric volume scattering, and moisture sensitivity independent of optical illumination.

cases.question: Compare VV and VH evidence for likely urban or vegetated regions.
cases.notes: Tests polarization channel analysis. Co-polarized VV responds strongly to surface roughness and vertical structures, while cross-polarized VH responds predominantly to multiple volume scattering inside complex canopy structures.

cases.question: Analyze this scene using both optical and SAR imagery. Can the boundary between cultivated fields and seminatural vegetation be unambiguously identified?
cases.notes: Evaluates acknowledgment of uncertainty. Gradual transitions between pasture and mixed woodland create ambiguous boundaries where optical gradients and SAR speckle prevent dogmatic demarcation. Model must express appropriate epistemic uncertainty.

cases.question: Describe the spatial relationship between optical reflectance and SAR backscatter after reprojection to the geographic reference grid.
cases.expected_focus: spatial alignment across distinct CRS definitions to optical reference grid
cases.notes: Tests spatial alignment engine on real data when optical is in geographic coordinates (EPSG:4326) and SAR is in UTM projected coordinates (EPSG:32633). Validates target dimension matching and common grid alignment.
